news: Stock is down ~31% year-to-date and slipped another 3.05% today amid ongoing regulatory/lending-outlook concerns; price is now below its $18.18 weekly support level.
Launched SoFi Small Business Loans (up to $250K) and an AI-powered trading tool ('Composer'); also rolled out a new options-income ETF (SFYI).
Q2 earnings due July 29 - investors watching cross-sell and member-growth trends for signs of a turn.
Refinanced $46.9M convertible note into a smaller $16.9M convert plus a $30M term loan, cutting convertible principal ~64% and improving liquidity via a new $21.6M aircraft-backed facility.
New Chairman Shawn Pelsinger takes over July 24, 2026, succeeding Carl Albert (who becomes Chairman Emeritus).

Wheels Up signed as launch customer for Enterprise BrokerOS (SurfOS), a 2-3 year deal worth up to $12M in subscription revenue; independent risk models still flag an ~85% financial-distress probability.
Down 8.96% today and ~31% over the past month; price has broken below its $27.39 weekly support level on customer-concentration and AI-debt-financing concerns.
FY2026 Q4/full-year earnings call set for July 27, 2026 after market close.
Street remains largely Strong Buy (14-analyst median target ~$74.50); Craig-Hallum's Sutton reiterated Buy on July 2 despite the pullback.
Expanding into healthcare via the Diligent Robotics acquisition (doubling footprint to 44 cities) and into laundry delivery via a NoScrubs pilot.
Q1 2026 revenue grew 578% YoY to $3M and FY2026 guidance was reaffirmed at $26M, but opex tripled to $42.8M with a $49M net loss ($197.4M cash on hand).
Shares have roughly halved YTD and are down ~25% over 3 months; now trading below its $5.73 weekly support level.
Today's 9.4% drop follows a real overhang: the FDA is formally recommending against compounding pharmacies manufacturing certain peptides, with a PCAC review of seven peptides scheduled July 23-24.
BofA and Canaccord Genuity had raised price targets days earlier (Canaccord to $40 from $32) on accelerating Q2 sales trends and a new $400M JPMorgan financing facility.
Q2 earnings scheduled for August 10, 2026.
Q2 FY2026 earnings due July 22, 2026 (6 days out) after market close; consensus expects $0.86 EPS on $3.92B revenue (+22% YoY).
Options market is pricing a +/-13.3% move on the earnings print - a large potential swing for a 13.1%-of-portfolio position.
Stock is down ~51% over the past year; FY2026 guidance implies +17.7% EPS growth and +21.9% revenue growth.

S&P Global downgraded Oracle's credit rating to BBB- from BBB; stock has fallen 7 of the last 10 days (-9.6% over that span) and dropped another 6.2% today, breaking below its $126.11 weekly support level.

FY2026 results showed cloud revenue +47% to $9.9B (IaaS +93%) plus $67B in new AI infrastructure contracts signed in the quarter - fundamentals remain strong even as the stock is repriced for financing risk.
Next earnings not until Sept 8, 2026; Street remains largely Buy-rated despite the credit downgrade.
